races.title: State Assembly, District 48
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Blanca Rubio
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 48 (eastern San Gabriel Valley) since 2016. Former elementary school teacher of about 16 years. Served on the Baldwin Park Unified School District Board of Education from 2003 to 2016. Chairs the Assembly Governmental Organization Committee.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California and California Young Democrats endorsed her in the 2026 election, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions from Rubio that clearly bear on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police funding, gun policy, abortion, or school choice. We found no documented public stance on data centers or new development. We found no news reporting of controversies and no documented foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so her own answers on issues are unavailable. Her campaign site lists issue areas (women's issues, education and youth, housing and homelessness, domestic violence, climate change) but gave no specific positions.

local.label: Roots 80: She was born in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, and returned to Los Angeles with her family in 1977 as a child (born 1969). She has since lived in Baldwin Park and worked in the San Gabriel Valley and Fontana.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2016 (10 years). Baldwin Park school board member 2003-2016, including time as president and vice president. About 16 years as an elementary school teacher. Holds a business administration degree and a master's in education.
qual.why: Ten years of prior legislative service and more than a decade of local elected office put her in the high range for writing law and budgets. Her background is education and local government rather than a law or budget career, so she scores below the top. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

cands.name: Dan T. Tran
cands.bio: Real estate professional, known as "The Title Man." He says he spent 19 years as a title sales manager at Fidelity National Title. Republican candidate for California Assembly District 48 in 2024 and 2026. He has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California among the endorsements and voter guide recommendations he received in 2026. It also lists several voter-guide groups and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Dan Tran holding public office, so there is no voting or legislative record. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. His 2024 survey answers were general (education, small business, homeownership, community safety) and did not address data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth limits, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school choice. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties. His work history comes only from his own survey answers and was not independently confirmed. We could not confirm when his family moved to Glendora.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Los Angeles; he attended Glendora High School and Citrus College, and says his mother brought him to Glendora, he attended Glendora schools and he is raising his own children there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Real estate professional; by his own account, 19 years as a top-producing title sales manager at Fidelity National Title. He has no prior elected office.
qual.why: A business and management career in real estate fits the middle band. There is no legislative, policy or budget work on record, and the work history comes from his own survey answers.
